sentence: The HbA1c test shows average blood glucose over the past two to three months and is used to diagnose and monitor diabetes.
note: both: reflects average blood glucose over about 2 to 3 months

sentence: The HbA1c blood test reflects the average level of glucose in the blood over the past two to three months.
note: both

sentence: That is why it differs from a finger-prick reading, which captures one moment.
note: MedlinePlus (blended): differs from single finger-prick

sentence: Glucose attaches to a part of the red blood cell, and the more glucose there is in the blood, the more HbA1c is present.
note: Diabetes UK

sentence: Red blood cells live for about two to three months before new ones replace them, which sets the window the test covers.
note: MedlinePlus: red cells live 2-3 months; Diabetes UK says 8-12 weeks

sentence: Because it covers a longer window, the test does not show short-term rises or dips in glucose.
note: blended summary | edited after second pass

sentence: Doctors use it to diagnose diabetes.
note: Diabetes UK

sentence: They also use it to keep an eye on levels in people at risk of developing diabetes, a state called prediabetes.
note: Diabetes UK / MedlinePlus

sentence: In people who already have diabetes, it shows how well blood sugar has been controlled.
note: both

sentence: MedlinePlus says the test is not used to diagnose type 1 diabetes.
note: MedlinePlus (blended summary); second pass to confirm

sentence: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed with blood tests, and HbA1c is the usual first test.

sentence: HbA1c is not used to diagnose diabetes during pregnancy.

sentence: UK laboratories give HbA1c in millimoles per mole, while some countries use a percentage.

sentence: A higher target may suit someone who has had many problems with low blood glucose.

sentence: As people age, the diabetes team may raise the target, because the risks of tight control can outweigh the benefits.

sentence: NICE patient information advises that HbA1c is usually tested every three to six months.

sentence: It may be done more often if blood glucose levels are changing quickly.

sentence: Once blood glucose is stable, NICE patient information says the test is usually every six months.

sentence: Conditions that affect red blood cells can make the result less accurate, such as anaemia or an uncommon form of haemoglobin.

sentence: Where HbA1c is unreliable, glucose-based blood tests are used for diagnosis instead.

sentence: Pregnancy, heavy bleeding and recent blood transfusion can also make HbA1c unreliable.

sentence: An NHS Scotland resource says the HbA1c may change if diet, physical activity, weight or medication have changed.

sentence: An estimated average glucose converts HbA1c into meter units, but it is an average and not an exact match for readings.

sentence: Heavy bleeding or haemolytic anaemia can make HbA1c falsely low, while iron deficiency may raise it.

sentence: Some haemoglobin variants can interfere with HbA1c measurement, so other methods may be needed.

sentence: A GP can refer eligible people to the free NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme, and some areas allow self-referral.

sentence: People with an intermediate result are usually monitored at least once a year.

sentence: A GP appointment is the route to discuss any result.
